BRIEF STATEMENT OF REASONS FOR DECISION:
1.

Briefly, the allegations of the prosecution are that on 31.05.2019 at 10.05 PM time, near Tatiksha Public School Sec 11 Rohini Delhi accused was found driving vehicle bearing no. DL-9CAM-2431 in a State vs Mange Ram on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107395216/
1 manner so rashly or negligently as to endanger human life and personal safety of others and thereby accused had committed an offence punishable U/s 279 IPC.

Further, on the aforesaid date and place while driving so, hit his vehicle to the pedestrian and he fell down on the road and succumbed to death and thereby accused had committed an offence punishable U/s 304 A IPC within the cognizance of this court.
2.
Investigation was conducted into the allegations.
Upon completion thereof, charge sheet was filed.
The accused was summoned.
Compliance of section 207 Cr.P.C. was done by providing copy of the charge sheet and annexed documents to the accused.
3. Upon finding a prima facie case against the accused, notice for the offences punishable U/s 279/304 A IPC was framed against the accused.
The accused pleaded not guilty and claimed trial.
4. In order to substantiate the allegations, following witnesses have been examined on behalf of the prosecution.

5. PW-1 Arun Kumar Soni has deposed that he is presently doing job State Vs Mange Ram FIR no.

PW-1 further deposed that he does not remember anything regarding the present case due to lapse of time as well as his family related problems.
PW-1 further deposed that he cannot identify the accused and the offending vehicle due to the lapse of the time.
6. Since the PW-1 Arun Kumar Soni had turned hostile, thereafter with the permission of the court he was cross-examined by Ld. APP for the State as he was resiling from his previous statement.

PW-1 denied the suggestion that on 31.05.2019, he was at his in laws home (sasural home) situated at Sector 11 Rohini Delhi and after eating food, he alongwith his brother in law namely Manish Gautam (deceased) went for walk and when they reached Titiksha Public School Sector 11 Rohini at around 9:45 pm one vehicle bearing no DL 9CAN 2431 came from back in rash, negligent and speedy way and hit his brother in law and due to same his brother in law fell on the road and received injuries.
PW-1 further denied the suggestion that the name of the accused was revealed as Mange Ram.
PW-1 further denied the suggestion that he brought his car at the spot and took his brother in law to Max Hospital Shalimar Bagh.
PW-1 failed to identify the accused and photographs of the offending vehicle.
Thereafter, PW-1 was duly cross examined by Ld. counsel for accused.

7. Law relating to hostile witness has been categorically discussed by the Apex Court in the case titled as Sat Pal vs Delhi Administration 1976 AIR 294, 1976 SCR (2) 11:
"From the above conspectus, it emerges clear that even in a Digitally signed by SARTHAK SARTHAK PANWAR PANWAR Date:
2025.08.07 State Vs Mange Ram FIR no. 239/2019 5 of 5 17:52:11 +0530 criminal prosecution when a witness is cross-examined and contradicted with the leave of the court, by the party calling him, his evidence cannot, as a matter of law, be treated as washed off the record altogether.

It is for the Judge of fact to consider in each case State vs Mange Ram on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/107395216/
2 whether as a result of such cross-examination and contradiction the witness stands thoroughly discredited or can still be believed in regard to a part of his testimony.

entities.text: State vs Mange Ram on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
If the Judge finds that in the process, the credit of the witness has not been completely shaken, he may, after reading and considering the evidence of the witness, as a whole,
with due caution and care, accept, in the light of the other evidence on the record that part of his testimony which he finds to be credit worthy and act upon it.

If in a given case, the whole of the testimony of the witness is impugned, and in the process the witness stands squarely and totally discredited, the Judge should, as a matter of prudence, discard his evidence in toto."

Since the star witness of the present case i.e. PW Arun Kumar Soni had turned hostile in toto and failed to identify the accused and photographs of offending vehicle, therefore, remaining witnesses were also dropped from list of witnesses as they were formal in nature and examining them would have been a futile exercise at the cost of judicial time and resources as their testimonies, even if accepted unrebutted, would not have been sufficient to prove the guilt of the accused person.

Hence,
PE was ultimately closed, in view of the observations of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India in case titled as Satish Mehra Vs. Delhi Administration and Anr: 1996 JCC 507.

sentences.text: 8. Final arguments were heard and record of the case has been perused.
9. It is the cardinal principle of criminal justice delivery system that the prosecution has to prove the guilt of accused beyond reasonable doubts.
No matter how weak the defence of accused is but, the golden rule of the criminal jurisprudence is that the case of the prosecution has to stand on its own legs.

10. Since the star witness of the present case i.e. PW Arun Kumar Soni had turned hostile in toto and failed to identify the accused and photographs of offending vehicle, therefore the remaining witnesses were also dropped from list of witnesses as they were formal in nature who were not present at the place of incident.
Hence, this court does away with the necessity of recording testimonies of remaining formal prosecution witnesses and recording statement of accused (SA).

Since no incriminating evidence against the accused has been brought on record by the prosecution,
therefore, the prosecution has failed to prove its case beyond reasonable doubts.
Accordingly, this court acquits the accused Mange Ram S/o Sh. Mehar Singh of charges u/s 279/304 A IPC.
